g.text: NeuralForecast model argument, e.g. loss=MAE() or loss=HuberLoss(delta=5). Computed on the scaled target.

text.style: fill: #222222; font: 7.8px 'Helvetica Neue', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans'

g.text: What it does: MAE is minimized by the median of each forecast's distribution. Huber is squared for small errors and absolute for

text.style: fill: #222222; font: 7.8px 'Helvetica Neue', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans'

g.text: large ones, so it sits between the median and the mean; delta (in scaled units) sets where it switches.

text.style: fill: #222222; font: italic 7.8px 'Helvetica Neue', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start

g.text: Why it matters here: On intermittent series the median week is often zero, so a median forecast under-calls total volume.

g.text: Try on your data: Pick the loss by how you're scored: if total volume (bias) matters, avoid pure MAE; tune Huber's delta.

text.style: fill: #111111; font: 700 13.5px 'Helvetica Neue', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start

g.text: With a point loss, use Huber, not MAE: bias -9.8% → -3.6%

text.style: fill: #555555; font: 8px 'Helvetica Neue', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans'

g.text: N-HiTS, 30,490 M5 weekly series, single seed. Only this setting differs between the two columns.

text.style: fill: #555555; font: 8px 'Helvetica Neue', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans'

g.text: Black = actuals; colored = 13-week forecasts from 3 origins (one fit at the first origin). Numbers cover all series.
